implementation_notes: Go replaces the classic record set with a typed slice: db.QueryContext returns *sql.Rows - a live cursor, not a value - and the idiomatic hand-over is to Scan each row into a struct and append it to []T, checking rows.Err() afterwards. What replaces the RecordSet class is therefore the slice plus its struct; column metadata is available (rows.Columns(), rows.ColumnTypes()) but is normally consumed only by generic tooling. Reach for []map[string]any or a matrix of sql.RawBytes only when the projection truly is dynamic - the moment the shape is known, a struct slice is both the contract and the faster representation.
pitfalls: rows is a cursor over a pooled connection: forgetting defer rows.Close() (or returning mid-loop) leaks a connection, and skipping rows.Err() after the loop hides mid-iteration network errors.
Scanning SQL NULL into a non-nullable Go value fails with an error - use pointers, sql.NullString/sql.NullInt64, or make the column NOT NULL.
[]map[string]any loses the column contract, allocates a map per row and cannot be checked by the compiler; the struct slice is both faster and safer.
